name: Google Gemini
tagline: Google AI assistant bundled with Gemini Advanced and Google AI Pro

pricing.notes: Official Google subscriptions page checked 2026-07-30; Google AI Pro listed at $19.99/month.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 15 GB storage; exact prompt limits vary; short-term limits generally refresh after 5 hours and some features also have weekly limits.

tiers.name: Google AI Plus
tiers.limits: About 2× Free usage; 200 monthly AI credits for Flow; 400 GB storage.
tiers.notes: Google offers monthly and yearly billing, but the current US annual amount was not exposed on the public page.

tiers.name: Google AI Pro
tiers.limits: About 4× Free usage; 1,000 monthly AI credits; 5 TB storage; 1M-token context.
tiers.notes: Google offers monthly and yearly billing, but the current US annual amount was not exposed on the public page.

tiers.name: Google AI Ultra 5x
tiers.limits: About 5× Pro usage; 10,000 monthly AI credits; 20 TB storage.

tiers.name: Google AI Ultra 20x
tiers.limits: About 20× Pro usage; 25,000 monthly AI credits; 30 TB storage.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 15 GB storage; prompt and feature limits are variable rather than fixed public counts
pricing.billingTerms: Plus and Pro support monthly + annual billing (annual US amount not publicly exposed); Ultra is monthly only
pricing.hiddenCosts: Additional AI-credit packs are sold. Google One bundle overlap can create duplicate storage/benefits, and partial-period refunds are generally not provided.

verdictSummary: A chat UI is easy, but Gemini's model access, Google ecosystem integration, multimodality, storage tie-ins, and platform distribution are not solo-buildable.
coreLoopDIY: Build a multi-model chat app with document upload and optional Google API integrations.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay for model access and Google-native placement, not because chat UIs are hard.

priorArt.name: Open WebUI
priorArt.desc: Open-source self-hosted chat UI for model APIs and local models.

alternatives.name: AnythingLLM
alternatives.desc: A private AI desk for documents and agents; install it, then choose local models or somebody else's meter.

facts.install: Desktop installer for macOS/Windows/Linux, or Docker for a self-hosted web instance
facts.engines: Local llama.cpp models plus Ollama, LM Studio, LocalAI and many cloud APIs including OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, Azure, OpenRouter and Mistral
facts.dataFormat: Desktop data stays in the app's local storage; self-hosted data is stored in the mounted server storage and chosen vector database (LanceDB by default), while prompts sent to cloud models leave the machine
facts.gapVsPaid: It cannot reproduce Gemini's first-party Gmail, Docs, Drive, Android, and Google Search integration, and it includes no Google AI Pro model quota.
facts.setupBlocker: The installer is easy, but useful results still require downloading a local model or supplying a model-provider API key

alternatives.name: Big-AGI
alternatives.desc: A local-first multi-model workspace with files, search, code and personas; the interface assumes you enjoy buttons.

facts.install: Use the hosted web app with your API keys, or self-host with Docker/Vercel
facts.engines: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Azure, Bedrock, DeepSeek, Groq, Mistral, OpenRouter, Perplexity, Together, xAI, Ollama, LocalAI, LM Studio and OpenAI-compatible endpoints
facts.dataFormat: The open app stores chats and settings locally in the browser by default; hosted Pro adds synced cloud storage, and model requests go to whichever provider the user configures
facts.gapVsPaid: It supplies a multi-model interface but not Gemini's included model allowance or first-party integration across Google Search, Gmail, Docs, Drive, and Android.
facts.setupBlocker: The free hosted app is immediate, but it does not include model usage: the user must bring provider API keys and understand provider billing

alternatives.name: Cherry Studio
alternatives.desc: A desktop model switchboard with assistants, files, agents and MCP; bring keys or make your laptop sweat.

facts.install: Download the signed desktop installer for macOS, Windows or Linux
facts.engines: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and many other cloud APIs; Claude, Perplexity and Poe web integrations; local models through Ollama or LM Studio; OpenAI-compatible endpoints
facts.dataFormat: Chats, assistants and settings are stored in the desktop app's local profile; optional WebDAV backup/sync and cloud model calls copy relevant content to those services
facts.gapVsPaid: It makes you supply each model and account yourself and cannot match Gemini's first-party integration across Google's apps and services.
facts.setupBlocker: The app installs cleanly, but the first useful chat requires an API key or a separately installed local model server

alternatives.name: Jan
alternatives.desc: A local-first desktop assistant with cloud connectors and tools; your RAM gets the invoice.

facts.install: Download the macOS, Windows or Linux desktop installer
facts.engines: Built-in local inference via llama.cpp/llama-server plus OpenAI-compatible APIs and connectors such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Groq, Mistral and OpenRouter
facts.dataFormat: Threads, assistants, settings and downloaded model files live in Jan's local data folder; only requests sent to configured cloud providers leave the machine
facts.gapVsPaid: It can provide local or bring-your-own-model chat, but not Gemini's included frontier-model access or native Google ecosystem integration.
facts.setupBlocker: Local use requires downloading a multi-gigabyte model and enough RAM; cloud use requires an API key

alternatives.name: LibreChat
alternatives.desc: A self-hosted model switchboard with agents, files and tools; free software, paid model bills if you use paid models.

facts.install: Clone the repository and start the recommended Docker Compose stack
facts.engines: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini/Vertex AI, Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Mistral, Groq, OpenRouter, DeepSeek and custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints, plus agents and MCP
facts.dataFormat: Conversations, users and configuration live in MongoDB; search indexes use Meilisearch, uploaded/RAG content uses bundled storage and a vector database; prompts sent to cloud models leave the host
facts.gapVsPaid: It adds server administration and separate model bills while still lacking Gemini's native Gmail, Docs, Drive, Search, and Android integration.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker Compose brings several services, and the default MongoDB image does not run on Apple Silicon without changing the setup

alternatives.name: LM Studio
alternatives.desc: A local-model desktop lab with chat, documents and tools; free forever, but your hardware is now the cloud.

facts.install: Download the macOS, Windows or Linux desktop installer
facts.engines: Runs GGUF models through llama.cpp and MLX models on Apple Silicon; downloads models from Hugging Face and exposes local OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs
facts.dataFormat: Chats, attached documents, presets and downloaded model weights stay in LM Studio's local application data; local chat and RAG can run fully offline
facts.gapVsPaid: It is a local-model laboratory, so live web grounding, Google's frontier models, and tight integration with Google apps are the main losses.
facts.setupBlocker: The installer is clean, but the user must choose and download a model large enough for the task and small enough for their RAM

alternatives.name: Open WebUI
alternatives.desc: ChatGPT-shaped self-hosting with models, files, search and tools; the software is free, the admin role is yours.

facts.install: Run the official Docker image, install the Python package, or deploy with Kubernetes
facts.engines: Ollama and any OpenAI-compatible API, including LM Studio, vLLM, Groq, Mistral and OpenRouter; additional speech, image and search providers
facts.dataFormat: By default, chats and account data live in a local SQLite webui.db, uploads in a data/uploads directory and embeddings in the configured vector store; PostgreSQL and object storage are optional
facts.gapVsPaid: It can imitate the chat surface, but it does not include Gemini usage or Google's first-party Search, Workspace, and Android integrations.
facts.setupBlocker: A non-expert must install Docker or a compatible Python environment, mount persistent storage correctly, and separately provide Ollama or an API endpoint

alternatives.name: LobeHub
alternatives.desc: A polished agents-and-files workspace; self-hosting is free and frontier inference usually is not.

facts.install: Use the hosted service, or self-host with Docker Compose or a supported cloud deployment template
facts.engines: OpenAI-compatible providers plus OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, Azure, OpenRouter, Ollama and other local/cloud model endpoints
facts.dataFormat: Hosted data lives in LobeHub's cloud; self-hosted deployments use PostgreSQL for app data and S3-compatible object storage for files, with model prompts also sent to the configured provider
facts.gapVsPaid: It offers a polished model workspace but not Gemini's bundled model capacity or first-party integration with Google's consumer and Workspace products.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting now means configuring Docker plus PostgreSQL, authentication and S3-compatible storage rather than launching a single stateless container

rejectedAlternatives.name: Msty
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The desktop core is $0, but the terms limit it to private non-commercial use; paid work needs a license.

notes: Completes the model-platform set; useful comparison for structural no verdicts.
prompt:
Build me a personal chat client on the Gemini API to replace my Google AI Pro
subscription with per-token billing. Requirements:

- A local web app: Node + Express + better-sqlite3, one page, binds to
  localhost.
- Gemini API key in .env, with optional Claude and OpenAI keys too; a model
  picker per conversation.
- Streaming responses with Markdown and code-block rendering; history in SQLite
  with FTS5 search across old conversations.
- Upload PDFs and images and pass them through to models that accept them.
- System-prompt presets as .md files in ./prompts/, selectable per chat.
- Export any conversation to a Markdown file.
- No accounts, no telemetry; history stays on my machine, only prompts go to
  the APIs.
- Out of scope: Gmail, Docs, and Drive integrations, and mobile apps. Do not
  build Google Workspace OAuth; that ecosystem tie-in is the subscription.
- README: where to create each API key, a rough cost table per model, and state
  that per-token billing can land above or below $20/month depending on use,
  the model itself is only rentable.
